chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abī Mālik al-Juhanī, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUmārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who bought something from the covering of the House: may the dead person be shrouded in it? He said: “No.”

key_terms.كِسْوَةِ: the covering cloth, here referring to the covering of the Kaʿbah
key_terms.لَا: no; indicating prohibition or negation in response

ai.seo_question: Can a deceased person be shrouded in cloth bought from the covering of the Kaʿbah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that something purchased from the covering of the House is not to be used as a shroud for the deceased. It relates to funerary rulings and the proper limits concerning sacred items associated with the Kaʿbah.
